To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose two novel approaches to fast thermal analysis, i.e., moment matching based on spectrum analysis and piecewise constant power input, for efficient runtime temperature tracking and DTM.

the proposed thermal moment matching methods are based on the observation of strong periodicity of the power consumption and average power consumption of microprocessors, and the proposed thermal moment analysis algorithm can be applied to online temperature tracking with low overhead and high accuracy, and can also be applied to runtime thermal management with low overhead and fast response time.

(1) the power consumption of microprocessors running typical workload exhibits strong periodic nature and the steady-state temperature response can be obtained by fast spectrum analysis of the power input; (2) the average power consumption determines the trend of transient temperature changes, and using piecewise constant power input can further speed up online thermal analysis; (3) the resulting thermal analysis algorithm is numerically stable and leads to 10-100 times speedup over the existing transient thermal simulation algorithms with small accuracy loss

the runtime temperature tracking and management of high-performance processors.
the runtime thermal management for microprocessors, where thermal analysis is a key component.
